download.title: Daily awareness, in your pocket
download.lead: Daily energy weather, prompts, journal and widgets live in the app; deep reports, pair invitations and the pro workspace live on the web. One account, synced everywhere.

combine6.detail: One of your branches combines with one of the other’s ({ap} and {bp} pillars): some layer of daily life simply fits, with an effortless understanding.

mutual.detail: Your five phases complement each other: what one lacks the other has in abundance, and each chart’s strongest phase is what the other needs. Together you both come into better balance — a rare structure.

one_way.detail: One person’s five phases supply exactly what the other needs: the one supplied feels steadier, and the one supplying deserves to be seen and given back to.

clash.detail: Your day branches clash: your routines, habits and rhythms of closeness differ, and it shows most once you share a home.

combine6.detail: Your day branches combine: your daily and intimate rhythms match, and living together feels like home.

clash.detail: Your day stems clash: everyday small things can turn into head-on collisions, and when you talk fast you push against each other — the same tension makes you hard to ignore.

combine.detail: Your day stems form one of the five combinations (transforming toward {el}): a natural affinity that can feel like meeting an old friend, and you drift toward each other without trying.

controls.detail: One person’s day stem restrains the other’s: one of you tends to become the other’s rules and pressure — sometimes exactly the containment the other needs. It comes down to how hard.

generates.detail: One person’s day stem feeds the other’s: one of you naturally nourishes and backs the other, who finds firmer footing in the relationship.

same_element.detail: Your day stems share an element ({sa}, {sb}): kindred temperaments that understand each other quickly — and, being alike, neither is keen to give way first.

output_meets_power.detail: One of you is in a breaking-out output decade while the other is in a pressured officer decade: you push each other hard, and can both be wound tight at once.

sync.detail: Your luck pillars point the same way for the next ten years: you rise and settle together and tend to want the same kinds of things at the same time.

sole_element.detail: Taken together, nearly all of your {el} comes from one person: when that person steps away the pair loses that strength, so it is worth turning it into shared agreements rather than leaving it in one head.
sole_element.phrase: {el} sits almost all on one side

both_emotional.detail: You both have emotional authority: big decisions need time for each of you, so agree on a cooling-off period and avoid deciding on the spot at a high or a low.

wave_vs_instant.detail: One of you needs the emotional wave to settle before seeing clearly, the other knows in the moment: one feels rushed, the other feels held back. Agreeing that big decisions wait a night helps more than any advice.

companionship.detail: You both hold {channels} whole: on that theme you run at the same frequency — easy as old friends, no explaining needed.

compromise.detail: On {channels}, one of you holds the whole channel and the other only one end: one tends to lead on that theme while the other gives way, and small grievances can build up.

dominance.detail: {channels} lives in only one of you: that person brings energy the other lacks, which the other can learn from — while taking care not to be swept along by it.

many.detail: Each of you holds one end, and together you complete {channels}: you fill each other in, being close feels like being switched on, and the pull comes from difference rather than likeness.

some.detail: Together you complete {channels}: on that theme you attract and complete each other.

throat.detail: Several of your electromagnetic channels run through the Throat: together, ideas get said and made more easily — a pairing built for expressing and creating together.

few.detail: Together you leave almost no center open: you are rarely bored and rarely quiet as a pair, so each of you needs some time alone to come back to yourself.

shared.detail: Several centers stay open even together: these are the themes where the outside world can sway you both — and good ground to practise on together.

manifestor_generator.detail: One of you can initiate without waiting, the other commits for the long haul once responding: the natural split is one starts, one goes deep — as long as the starter informs first and the other checks in first.

projector_generator.detail: One of you needs an invitation before offering a view, the other needs something to respond to before moving: who speaks first often decides where things go.
projector_generator.phrase: Waiting to be invited × waiting to respond

two_manifestors.detail: You are both types who can start things on your own: each wants to begin on your own timing, and telling each other in advance saves a lot of friction.

lifepath_lead_support.detail: One of your life paths leans toward leading and mastery, the other toward partnership and care: naturally complementary roles — just make sure the same person is not always the one giving way.

personal_year_same.detail: You are in the same personal year: this year runs at the same rhythm for you both — good for starting or wrapping things up together.

same_life_path.detail: You share a life path number: your life themes are alike, and it is easy to understand what the other is reaching for.

anxious_avoidant.detail: When uneasy, one of you moves closer and seeks reassurance while the other steps back for space: a chase-and-retreat loop that slows down once you both can see it.

both_anxious.detail: You both care a lot about each other’s responses: close times hold you both, and busy or quiet stretches can unsettle you both at once. A simple agreed “I’m here” signal helps.

both_avoidant.detail: You both lean towards independence and tend to process things on your own: you give each other room and it feels easy — and when it matters, remember to say “I need you”.

secure_anchor.detail: One of you has a secure attachment style: the relationship has a steady anchor, making it easier to find your way back to each other after ups and downs.

conscientiousness_gap.detail: One of you is orderly and punctual, the other spontaneous and flexible: chores, plans and punctuality are common sources of friction.

neuroticism_gap.detail: One of you feels strongly and notices early, the other stays even: the steady one can be an anchor — as long as the other’s feelings are not waved off as overthinking.

both_dominance.detail: You both like to make the call and push ahead: together you have plenty of drive, and when you disagree things can lock up. Agreeing in advance who decides what helps.

pace_gap.detail: One of you likes to move fast and adjust on the way, the other prefers to think it through and go steadily: the pace gap is a common rub — agreeing up front on when to decide makes it much smoother.

same_center.detail: Your Enneagram types share a center: your first reactions under stress are alike, so it is easy to see why the other acts as they do.

ei_split.detail: One of you needs to mull things over inside, the other needs to talk to think: on the same issue, one wants quiet while the other wants to discuss it now.
ei_split.phrase: Mull it over × talk it out

jp_split.detail: One of you likes to settle things early, the other to keep options open: plans, schedules and deadlines are the usual sticking points.

shared_intuition.detail: You both lean intuitive (N): you love talking about possibilities and meaning, and one of you picks up an idea the moment the other starts it.

shared_sensing.detail: You both lean toward sensing (S): you trust concrete facts and experience, and practical conversations go efficiently.

sn_split.detail: One of you sees patterns and possibilities first, the other facts and details: each can find the other too airy or too fussy — together you see the whole thing.

tf_split.detail: One of you weighs people and relationships first, the other logic and consistency: in an argument one feels unheard and the other feels unconvinced — and each is holding half of the picture.

opposite_direction.detail: What each of you values most sits opposite on the values circle: what one weighs heavily, the other weighs less. It lets each of you see the other side — talking through what matters to each before big decisions helps.

shared_direction.detail: Your values assessments point in a similar direction: many choices need no explaining — the other already knows why you make them.

dasha_sync.detail: (Reference) Your current main Dasha rulers are the same or friendly: this chapter of life carries similar themes for you both.

gana_low.detail: (Reference) Your Moon nakshatras fall in different temperament groups: traditionally a sign of differing moods and pace that asks for extra patience with each other.

gana_match.detail: (Reference) Your Moon nakshatras belong to compatible temperament groups (Gana): traditionally read as a similar everyday pace.

graha_maitri_high.detail: (Reference) The rulers of your Moon signs are friendly to each other: traditionally read as minds and hearts that meet easily.

tara_high.detail: (Reference) The Tara count between your nakshatras agrees: traditionally read as each being a help to the other.

yoni_high.detail: (Reference) Your nakshatras’ Yoni symbols agree: traditionally read as a strong instinctive closeness.

asc_asc_square.detail: Your Ascendants form a hard angle: you meet the world differently — one leads with harmony and mood, the other with structure and rules — so in public you can seem to pull in different directions.

jupiter_lifts.detail: One person’s Jupiter lights up the other’s Sun or Moon: around each other you grow more confident and more willing to dream, and the relationship widens your horizons.

mars_mars_tension.detail: Your two Mars placements oppose or square each other: you act at different speeds and in different styles, so when one wants to charge the other wants another approach — small things can spark arguments.

mercury_harmony.detail: Your Mercurys are in harmony: you think along similar lines, can finish each other’s half-sentences, and talking is a pleasure in itself.

mercury_tension.detail: Your Mercurys form a hard angle: you think and speak differently, so the same sentence can mean two things — worth asking “do you mean…?” more often.

moon_mc_conjunction.detail: One person’s Moon sits right on the other’s Midheaven (within {orb}°): emotional support flows naturally toward the other’s work and public life, often without needing to be said.

moon_moon_harmony.detail: Your Moons are in harmony: your emotional needs are alike, you want similar kinds of care when tired or low, and being together takes little effort.

moon_moon_tension.detail: Your Moons form a hard angle: you handle feelings differently, and the comfort one of you needs may be exactly what the other finds hardest to give.

node_contact.detail: One person’s personal planet sits on the other’s North Node: the relationship often feels like being drawn toward a direction you want but do not yet know.

overlay_7th.detail: One person’s Sun, Moon or Venus falls in the other’s 7th house: the other person is naturally seen in the role of partner.

pluto_personal.detail: One person’s Pluto touches the other’s personal planet: a deep, intense pull that can stir wanting control or fearing it — worth naming openly to each other.

saturn_moon.detail: One person’s Saturn presses on the other’s Moon: a strong sense of commitment and duty, which can leave one of you feeling managed and the other feeling leaned on.

saturn_sun_venus_soft.detail: One person’s Saturn harmonises with the other’s Sun or Venus: the bond has dependable structure and a long view, suited to things that take patience.

sun_mars_harmony.detail: One person’s Sun harmonises with the other’s Mars: your drives light each other up, and you both have more energy when you work on something together.

sun_moon_harmony.detail: One person’s Sun meets the other’s Moon in a conjunction or easy aspect: who one of you is becoming is exactly what makes the other feel at home.

uranus_venus_moon.detail: One person’s Uranus touches the other’s Venus or Moon: fresh, exciting and unpredictable — and in need of room for each of you to be free.

venus_mars_harmony.detail: One person’s Venus meets the other’s Mars in a conjunction or easy aspect: a classic pull, where one person’s charm sparks the other’s pursuit.

venus_mars_tension.detail: One person’s Venus squares or opposes the other’s Mars: strong attraction with a tug-of-war in it — you tend to want closeness in different ways and at different speeds.

ji_into_ming.detail: One person’s Obstruction transformation lands in the other’s Life or Partner palace: this person cares intensely and finds it hard to let go — too much caring can turn into pressure for both.

lu_into_ming.detail: One person’s Prosperity transformation lands in the other’s Life or Partner palace: this person naturally wants to give, and the other feels well treated.

ming_in_fude.detail: One person’s Life palace falls in the other’s Fortune palace: in this person’s company, the other feels inwardly at ease and mentally rested.
ming_in_fude.phrase: Life palace in the Fortune palace

ming_in_fumu.detail: One person’s Life palace falls in the other’s Parents palace: this person carries a mentor’s weight in the other’s eyes, and their advice tends to land.
ming_in_fumu.phrase: Life palace in the Parents palace

ming_in_fuqi.detail: One person’s Life palace falls in the other’s Partner palace: the moment one appears, the other naturally places them as a partner, with a hard-to-explain familiarity.
ming_in_fuqi.phrase: Life palace in the Partner palace

ming_in_guanlu.detail: One person’s Life palace falls in the other’s Career palace: in the other’s eyes this person is tied to work and goals — a good pairing for getting things done together.
ming_in_guanlu.phrase: Life palace in the Career palace

ming_in_peers.detail: One person’s Life palace falls in the other’s siblings or friends palace: you relate like friends and companions — level and direct.
ming_in_peers.phrase: Life palace in a peer palace

ming_in_resources.detail: One person’s Life palace falls in the other’s Wealth or Property palace: you tend to build resources and a home together.
ming_in_resources.phrase: Life palace in a resource palace

mutual_qianyi.detail: Each of your Life palaces falls in the other’s Travel palace: you are each other’s door to the wider world, and after meeting, both your worlds grow larger.

attraction.describes: What draws each of you toward the other.
attraction.name: Attraction

communication.describes: How easily ideas and words move between you.
communication.name: Communication

emotion.describes: How you catch each other’s feelings.
emotion.name: Emotional bond

growth.describes: How each of you helps the other grow more whole.
growth.name: Growth

rhythm.describes: Whether your pace for deciding, acting and resting matches.
rhythm.name: Rhythm

values.describes: How close the things you care about and the directions you value are.
values.name: Values

friction.body: You come close in different ways and at different speeds, and the more you care, the more you tug. Seeing the tug-of-war brings you closer than pretending it isn’t there.
friction.practice: Next time you feel the tug, each say in one sentence, “What I want right now is…”.
friction.quote: The pull is strong, and so is the tug-of-war.

quiet.body: On the charts, the signals of attraction between you are modest. Bonds like this often grow slowly out of familiarity and trust.
quiet.practice: Do one small new thing together, and notice how each of you shows up in it.
quiet.quote: Your bond runs on time, not sparks.

strong.body: The pull often comes from what each of you lacks in yourself. It draws you together — and makes you curious about why the other is so different.
strong.practice: Each write down the one quality in the other that draws you most, then swap and read.
strong.quote: There’s a pull between you that’s hard to ignore.

friction.body: You think and speak differently, and misunderstandings often begin with “I thought you meant…”. One extra question can save a whole argument.
friction.practice: Next time you feel misunderstood, first ask, “Did you mean…?” before responding.
friction.quote: The same sentence means two things between you.

quiet.body: The charts show few strong communication links between you. That doesn’t mean you can’t talk — just that it takes more deliberate expressing and checking.
quiet.practice: Set a regular weekly talk, and each share the one thing that mattered most to you that week.
quiet.quote: Your communication needs a little more intention.

strong.body: Ideas flow easily between you; one starts and the other picks it up. Because it’s so easy, you sometimes assume the other understood when they didn’t.
strong.practice: After discussing something important, ask the other to say it back in their own words.
strong.quote: When you talk, you often get it at once.

friction.body: The comfort one of you needs may be exactly what the other finds hardest to give. Telling “what I need” apart from “what I assume you need” is your practice.
friction.practice: Each write down “the one thing I most want you to do when I’m low,” then swap.
friction.quote: You handle feelings in different ways.

quiet.body: The charts show few strong emotional links between you. Depth of feeling often comes from what you live through together, not just from how you were born.
quiet.practice: Remember together one small, unforgettable moment you shared, and each describe how it felt.
quiet.quote: Your emotional bond is growing slowly.

strong.body: You catch each other’s feelings, and when things are hard the other is often the first person you think of. That comfort needs saying out loud so it isn’t taken for granted.
strong.practice: This week, each tell the other once: “When you’re here, I feel…”.
strong.quote: Around each other, your hearts settle.

friction.body: This relationship has a strong push, often carrying you both beyond your comfort zones. When the push gets to be too much, remember to give each other room to breathe.
friction.practice: This week, ask the other, “Is there anything you’d like me to push less on lately?”
friction.quote: You push each other, and sometimes wind each other up.

quiet.body: The charts show few strong signals of pushing each other to grow. A relationship like this is more of a harbour — a place to rest after time out in the world.
quiet.practice: Each share one way you want to grow this year, and ask how the other could support you.
quiet.quote: Your growth can happen side by side.

strong.body: What one of you has is what the other needs, and together you’re each more balanced. That complement also means learning from each other, not just leaning on each other.
strong.practice: Each write “Because of you, I’ve learned…”, then swap and read.
strong.quote: You help each other become more whole.

friction.body: One of you wants fast, the other slow; one wants to settle it, the other to keep looking. The practice isn’t changing each other but agreeing on a pace you can both live with.
friction.practice: Agree on one rule for big decisions — say, “we decide after sleeping on it” — and try it for a month.
friction.quote: Your rhythms run opposite — and nobody’s wrong.

quiet.body: The charts show no strong sync or clash in your rhythms. Keeping your own paces while holding some regular shared time is enough.
quiet.practice: Agree on one fixed shared slot each week, and plan the rest separately.
quiet.quote: It’s fine for your rhythms to run separately.

strong.body: You decide, act and rest at similar speeds, so living and working together takes little effort. Being in sync also means tensing up together — watch for each other’s tiredness.
strong.practice: Once a month, plan a half-day together with nothing on it.

friction.body: On some important things your priorities differ, and you can talk past each other. The difference isn’t the problem — leaving it unspoken is.
friction.practice: Pick one thing you disagree on, and each finish the sentence, “This matters to me because…”.

quiet.body: The charts show few strong value links. Many shared directions form slowly through one concrete choice after another.
quiet.practice: Next time you choose something together, each name what matters most to you first, then talk it through.
quiet.quote: Your values will line up through living together.

strong.body: On things that matter, you often end up on the same side without explaining. That ease makes shared decisions lighter — and it’s worth checking now and then that you still agree.
strong.practice: Each write down the three things that matter most over the next three years, and compare the overlap.
strong.quote: You care about very similar things.

closeness_vs_space.practice: Agree that whoever needs space says when they’ll be back, and whoever feels uneasy says so directly.
closeness_vs_space.scene: Under pressure, one of you moves closer for reassurance and the other steps back for space. The more one chases, the more the other retreats — and the other way round.

closer.inner: When the other pulls back, I start worrying I did something wrong, so I want reassurance even more.
closer.say: “I’m feeling a bit uneasy — could you just tell me we’re okay?”

spacer.inner: I need some space to come back to myself, and the harder I’m chased, the more I want to hide.
spacer.say: “I need an hour on my own, and then I’ll come and find you.”

closeness_vs_space.title: Closeness or space

control_vs_yield.practice: Once a month, check together: of recent decisions, which ones did each of you lead?
control_vs_yield.scene: On one theme, the same person always decides and the other goes along, and small grievances pile up over time.

leads.inner: I just want things done well; I hadn’t noticed the other has been giving way all along.
leads.say: “What’s your view on this? I’d like to hear what you really think.”

yields.inner: Speaking up feels like it’ll cause a fight, so I go along — though I see it differently inside.
yields.say: “This time I’d like to try it my way.”

control_vs_yield.title: Lead or follow

decision_pace.practice: Agree that big decisions wait a night, and set a specific time for the answer.
decision_pace.scene: When a big decision comes up, one of you knows right away and the other needs time for the feelings to settle. One feels rushed; the other feels held back.

fast.inner: I already know the answer, and waiting feels like being stuck while the moment slips away.
fast.say: “My gut says this. How long do you need? I can wait until then.”

slow.inner: I’m not avoiding the decision; I’m just not clear yet. When I’m rushed I panic, and might agree to anything.
slow.say: “I need to sleep on it. By this time tomorrow, you’ll have my answer.”

decision_pace.title: Fast and slow decisions

direct_clash.practice: Agree on a pause word; when either says it, you both stop for five minutes.
direct_clash.scene: Over everyday things, when you talk fast you butt heads, and one sharp sentence brings on a sharper one.

either.inner: I just want to be clear, but the other’s tone feels like a challenge, so I push harder too.
either.say: “We’re both getting heated — let’s pause five minutes and pick this up again.”

direct_clash.title: Head-on collisions

processing_style.practice: Agree on a rhythm: fifteen quiet minutes apart first, then talk together.
processing_style.scene: When something happens, one of you needs to think quietly first, the other needs to talk it out right away. One feels interrogated; the other feels shut out.

inward.inner: I need to go over it inside first; talking right away only gets out half-formed thoughts.
inward.say: “I need a little time to think — can we talk tonight?”

outward.inner: I think by talking, and the other’s silence makes me feel shut out.
outward.say: “I’d like to think out loud for a bit — you don’t have to respond yet.”

processing_style.title: Processing styles

same_element_rivalry.practice: Split decision rights by area, and agree in advance who decides what.
same_element_rivalry.scene: You’re so alike that you both have strong views on the same thing, and neither is keen to give way first.

either.inner: I know the other gets me, so I’d rather they be the one to give way.
either.say: “Let’s go with yours this time, and I’ll decide next time.”

same_element_rivalry.title: Too alike to yield

structure_vs_flow.practice: Together, write a list of three must-keeps and the parts that can change.
structure_vs_flow.scene: Over plans, schedules and deadlines, one of you wants to settle things early and the other wants to keep room to move.

improviser.inner: A rigid plan suffocates me, and I’m afraid of missing chances that turn up.
improviser.say: “I’m happy to agree a framework — just leave me some room to adjust.”

planner.inner: Until it’s settled, it hangs over me and I can’t relax.
planner.say: “Let’s lock in the one or two biggest things and keep the rest flexible.”

structure_vs_flow.title: Plan or flow

who_speaks_first.practice: On important matters, agree that one of you invites the other’s view first — and take turns.
who_speaks_first.scene: Something’s stuck: one of you is waiting to be asked before offering a view, the other is waiting for a move or a question first. So both stay silent.

initiates.inner: I’m waiting for a signal — or I’ve already moved ahead without thinking to say so.
initiates.say: “What do you think? I’d really like your read on this.”

waits.inner: I actually see it clearly, but when I speak up unasked it often doesn’t land.
waits.say: “I have some thoughts on this — would you like to hear them?”

who_speaks_first.title: Who speaks first
